entries.name: Polly
entries.summary: Polly adopts the Open Source Maintenance Fee. The fee applies only to the next major version released after 16 Nov 2026; existing versions stay free. The source licence (BSD-3-Clause) doesn't change.
entries.whoPays: Companies earning at least US$20,000 from a product or project that uses Polly: US$20 per month. Direct references only; Polly brought in by another library (for example Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience) is exempt.

alternatives.note: Microsoft's resilience package uses Polly transitively, which the fee doesn't cover (MIT).
Stay on the current major version; existing versions are not subject to the fee.

entries.name: MediatR
entries.summary: From v13, MediatR is dual-licensed under RPL-1.5 and the Lucky Penny Software commercial licence. Earlier versions keep their original Apache-2.0 terms.
entries.whoPays: A paid licence is needed for commercial use above the free Community edition: free for companies under US$5M gross annual revenue, non-profits under US$5M budget, education and non-production use. A licence key is required either way.

entries.name: AutoMapper
entries.summary: From v15, AutoMapper is dual-licensed under RPL-1.5 and the Lucky Penny Software commercial licence. Earlier versions keep their original MIT terms.
entries.whoPays: A paid licence is needed for commercial use above the free Community edition: free for companies under US$5M gross annual revenue, non-profits under US$5M budget, education and non-production use. A licence key is required either way.

entries.name: MassTransit
entries.summary: MassTransit v9 is a commercial product from Massient; v9 packages use the Massient licence. The v8 line remains Apache-2.0.
entries.whoPays: Commercial use of v9 requires a Massient licence key; see massient.com for terms.

alternatives.note: Apache-2.0 line, still receiving patch releases (8.5.12 at the time of writing).

entries.name: FluentAssertions
entries.summary: From v8, FluentAssertions uses the Xceed Community Licence for non-commercial use; commercial use needs a paid Xceed licence. v7 remains Apache-2.0.
entries.whoPays: Any commercial use of v8+ requires a paid licence from Xceed (per developer, per year).

entries.name: QuestPDF
entries.summary: From 2023.4.0, QuestPDF is dual-licensed: a free Community MIT licence for eligible users and a paid Professional or Enterprise licence for everyone else. The 2022.12.x line is MIT.
entries.whoPays: Organisations with US$1M or more annual gross revenue, and public-sector bodies and publicly traded companies regardless of revenue. Free Community licence for individuals, small businesses under US$1M, non-profits, open-source projects and transitive dependency users.

entries.name: Six Labors (ImageSharp)
entries.summary: From ImageSharp 3, ImageSharp.Web 3, ImageSharp.Drawing 2 and Fonts 2, Six Labors packages use the Six Labors Split License: Apache-2.0 for qualifying users, a paid commercial licence for others. Earlier versions are Apache-2.0.
entries.whoPays: For-profit companies and individuals with US$1M or more annual gross revenue that reference a Six Labors package directly in closed-source software. Free under Apache-2.0 for open-source software, non-profits, companies under US$1M, and transitive use through an unrelated third-party package.

entries.name: EPPlus
entries.summary: From v5, EPPlus is licensed under the Polyform Noncommercial License 1.0.0, with a paid commercial licence from EPPlus Software. v4 and earlier are LGPL.
entries.whoPays: Any commercial use of v5 or later requires a paid EPPlus commercial licence. Polyform Noncommercial covers personal and non-commercial use only.

entries.name: Extended WPF Toolkit
entries.summary: From v4, the Extended WPF Toolkit uses the Xceed Community License Agreement, which allows non-commercial use only. v3.8.2 and earlier are MS-PL.
entries.whoPays: Any commercial use of v4 or later requires a paid licence from Xceed (Xceed Toolkit Plus).

alternatives.note: Community fork of the MS-PL toolkit (MS-PL).

entries.name: Blazorise
entries.summary: From 0.9.4.4, Blazorise packages use the Blazorise Software License Agreement: a free Community licence for individuals and a paid per-developer commercial licence. 0.9.4.3 and earlier are Apache-2.0.
entries.whoPays: Companies, non-profits, government bodies and freelancers doing client work, at any size (per developer). The free Community licence covers individuals only, with row and item limits on some components.

entries.name: NBomber
entries.summary: From v5, NBomber uses the NBomber Business License Agreement. Personal use is free; organisations need a paid licence. v4 and earlier are Apache-2.0.
entries.whoPays: Any organisation using NBomber v5 or later needs a licence (one licence covers the whole organisation). Free for personal use only.

entries.name: WiX Toolset
entries.summary: From v6, WiX Toolset binaries on NuGet come with an Open Source Maintenance Fee agreement. The source licence (MS-RL) doesn't change.
entries.whoPays: Users who generate revenue with WiX, paid by sponsoring wixtoolset on GitHub. Non-revenue use, and users who already pay the maintainers for support, are exempt.

alternatives.note: Last release without the maintenance fee.

entries.name: json-everything
entries.summary: From the February 2026 releases (JsonSchema.Net 9, JsonPath.Net 3, JsonPointer.Net 7 and the rest), json-everything packages come with an Open Source Maintenance Fee agreement. The source licence (MIT) doesn't change.
entries.whoPays: All organisations or users of any json-everything library who generate revenue with it, as a monthly fee. Non-revenue use, and users who already pay the maintainers at least the fee, are exempt.

alternatives.note: Built into .NET for JSON parsing and serialisation (MIT); no JSON Schema validation.

entries.name: Verify
entries.summary: Verify versions released after 1 Sep 2026 (v33 and later) come with an Open Source Maintenance Fee agreement, checked at build time. The source licence (MIT) doesn't change. Test-framework adapters such as Verify.XunitV3 stay MIT but depend on Verify.
entries.whoPays: Organisations using Verify in revenue-generating work with annual gross revenue of US$10,000 or more, and government agencies: US$5 to US$100 per month by organisation size, paid through GitHub Sponsors.

alternatives.note: Last release without the maintenance fee.

entries.name: ThisAssembly (Devlooped)
entries.summary: From 2.1.0, ThisAssembly packages come with an Open Source Maintenance Fee agreement. The source licence (MIT) doesn't change.
entries.whoPays: Users who generate revenue with the packages, paid by sponsoring Devlooped on GitHub at the OSMF tier. One fee covers all Devlooped packages.

alternatives.note: Last release without the maintenance fee.

entries.name: NPOI
entries.summary: From 2.8.0, NPOI packages come with an Open Source Maintenance Fee agreement. The source licence (Apache-2.0) doesn't change.
entries.whoPays: Users of NPOI in revenue-generating activities with annual gross revenue of US$10,000 or more, as a monthly fee through GitHub Sponsors.

alternatives.note: Last release without the maintenance fee.

entries.name: Duende IdentityServer
entries.lastFreeVersion: None. The free predecessor, IdentityServer4 (last release 4.1.2, Apache-2.0), is no longer supported.
entries.summary: Duende IdentityServer, the successor to IdentityServer4, is commercial software. A free Community Edition covers small companies and non-profits; development, testing and personal projects need no licence.
entries.whoPays: Organisations with US$1M or more projected annual gross revenue or US$3M or more in capital, non-profits with budgets of US$1M or more, and anyone redistributing IdentityServer to third parties. Others can apply for the free Community Edition licence key.

alternatives.note: OpenID Connect server and client for ASP.NET Core (Apache-2.0).
